source.title_on_document: Human–GenAI collaboration across creative phases: Cognitive mechanisms shaping novelty and usefulness

supplement.where: No separate supplementary material or online appendix is referenced. Appendices A-I are included in this PDF, pp. 11-14. Study 3 links an external AsPredicted preregistration (https://aspredicted.org/2hsq-9sg4.pdf, p. 7), whose contents are not included in the PDF. Attempts to retrieve that protocol and the publisher page with Python urllib were blocked by the environment's network permissions.
supplement.holds: The included appendices contain interview profiles and questions, the qualitative coding framework, tasks, manipulation materials, and scale items. No additional total-effect standard errors or confidence intervals are given there. Tables 1-2 give condition means, SDs, and within-person correlations for Studies 2a-2b; Table 3 gives pooled means, SDs, and phase-outcome correlations for Study 3, without arm means or cell sizes. The reported standard errors and confidence intervals for novelty/usefulness pathways concern indirect effects or moderated-mediation indices. The contents of the external preregistration could not be checked.

paper_design_summary: Study 1 comprised interviews with 20 creative professionals. Studies 2a (42 students analyzed) and 2b (44 students analyzed) are within-person lab experiments with two product proposals per participant in randomized order: one with GenAI allowed during a 10-minute phase (idea generation in 2a, idea elaboration in 2b) and one without AI; SparkDesk is named only for Study 2a, and three marketing experts rated novelty and usefulness (pp. 5-7, Appendices D-F). Study 3 is a preregistered online 2 x 2 experiment with 198 employees analyzed, randomly assigned to ChatGPT collaboration in the idea generation or elaboration phase crossed with high or low perceived GenAI intelligence; experts rated advertising proposals using the Study 2 approach (p. 7, Sections 6.1-6.2).

eligibility.reason: Study 3 alone meets all three criteria: individuals were randomly assigned to four conditions crossing the phase of ChatGPT collaboration with perceived GenAI intelligence (p. 7, Section 6.1), 198 people were analyzed after 7 attention-check exclusions from 205 recruited (p. 7, Section 6.1; p. 8, Table 3), and participants' proposals received expert novelty and usefulness ratings using the Study 2 approach (p. 7, Section 6.2; pp. 5-6, Section 5.1.2). The phase comparison is between two AI configurations (ai_design); no no-AI arm is required for this contrast. Unspecified AI access in the other phase affects the precise availability code, not the documented randomized assignment. Studies 2a and 2b each randomize condition order but analyze only 42 and 44 people, respectively, so neither meets the size criterion. Missing Study 3 cell counts, arm means, and total-effect standard errors limit extraction, not eligibility.

one_line_finding: Among 198 employees analyzed in Study 3, expert-rated novelty favors ChatGPT collaboration during idea generation and usefulness favors collaboration during elaboration (Table 3, p. 8: phase dummy 1 = elaboration, r = −0.30 and 0.42, respectively); the smaller Studies 2a and 2b report higher GenAI-condition novelty (6.05 vs 5.44; 42 analyzed; Table 1, p. 6) and usefulness (5.89 vs 5.49; 44 analyzed; Table 2, p. 7).
open_questions: Study 3 does not state whether ChatGPT was blocked during the non-assigned phase. Section 6.1 (p. 7) describes guided interactions during specific phases, while Appendix H (p. 14) gives only the perceived-intelligence manipulation. S4-O1 and S4-O2 therefore have ai_available_when_produced = null. The authors' phase instructions or system-access rules would settle this.

The paper describes expert ratings of creative proposals but does not explicitly identify whether preliminary ideas or final proposals were rated (pp. 5-7, Sections 5.1.2 and 6.2). Study 2a's mixed and Study 2b's yes availability codes describe the documented task sequences assuming the completed proposal was rated; Study 3 availability remains null. Author confirmation of the scored submission would settle the timing detail.

Study 3 gives 198 analyzed people but no arm/cell counts or arm-level novelty/usefulness means (p. 7, Section 6.1; p. 8, Table 3). Exact counts, means, and contrast precision require the authors' participant-level records or analysis outputs; no posted-data link is given.

The linked AsPredicted preregistration is absent from the PDF and could not be retrieved because network access was blocked. Its primary-outcome specification remains unconfirmed; the paper_primary codes follow the paper's hypotheses (pp. 3-4, p. 7).

Studies 2a and 2b print condition means, SDs, and within-person correlations but no paired total-effect test or standard error (Tables 1-2, pp. 6-7). The authors' analysis output would supply those tests if needed; the indirect-effect intervals are not precision for the total contrasts.

Study 3 reports no direct contrast of the randomized perceived-intelligence factor on novelty or usefulness; PGenAII in Table 3 is the measured scale (pp. 7-9). Factorial cell summaries or author analysis outputs would settle any additional output-level contrast.
notes: Cognitive flexibility and cognitive overload are self-reported mediators and are not listed as outcomes. Study 3's perceived-intelligence manipulation is reported as a moderator of indirect effects and cognitive overload, with no direct contrast on rated novelty or usefulness. All six outcome question codes remain with_ai: the scored creative proposal belongs to one task incorporating GenAI collaboration; Study 2a elaborates its AI-assisted preliminary ideas rather than beginning a separate unassisted task (Appendices D-E, p. 13). The exact rated submission is not explicitly identified, as recorded in open_questions. Study 3's AI-availability codes are null because the non-assigned-phase access rule is not stated; this supersedes the historical reconciliation's mixed coding. Study 2a used SparkDesk; Study 2b does not name its GenAI tool. Directions for Studies 2a and 2b come from the printed means; their within-person correlations are retained for later paired-precision work, without computing an effect size. Study 3's Table 3 correlations use Section 6.3.1's definition of CP (1 = elaboration, 0 = generation); H3 explicitly uses the opposite coding for its novelty mediation, so each reported statistic retains its local definition. The usefulness contrast now treats elaboration as treatment, consistent with H5, while novelty treats generation as treatment. For Study 3, standardized_effect denotes the printed phase-outcome correlation, not a computed standardized mean difference. The statistics_available fields describe only the output contrasts: arm_means_sds_ns for Studies 2a-2b and standardized_effect for Study 3. Indirect-effect and moderated-mediation confidence intervals remain labeled in reported as mechanism results and must not be converted into standard errors for total contrasts. Study 3's phase manipulation check is t(196) = 28.63, p < 0.001 (generation M = 6.31, SD = 0.89; elaboration M = 2.00, SD = 1.21), p. 8; the manipulation-index item is not printed. The reconciliation object is preserved unchanged as the earlier audit record; final records the finalizer's decisions.

challenge_resolution.locator: p. 6, Section 5.2.1; p. 13, Appendix F; p. 5, Section 5.1.1

challenge_resolution.problem: S4-O1 and S4-O2 code AI availability as mixed despite no explicit rule for ChatGPT access during the non-assigned phase.
challenge_resolution.what_changed: Removed the unsupported mixed values and set both availability fields to null. The source confirms collaboration during assigned phases but does not settle access during the other phase or the exact submission rated. Kept with_ai and documented the uncertainty in measure_detail and open_questions. This does not change any eligibility criterion.
challenge_resolution.quote: we developed a custom online system that guided participants’ interactions with GenAI during specific creative phases (Chen & Chan, 2024).

challenge_resolution.problem: S2-O1, S3-O1, S4-O1, and S4-O2 list confidence_interval as available for output contrasts although the intervals concern indirect effects.
challenge_resolution.what_changed: Removed confidence_interval from these four statistics_available arrays. Studies 2a-2b retain arm_means_sds_ns; Study 3 retains standardized_effect for the printed correlations. Kept the indirect-effect and moderated-mediation numbers explicitly labeled in reported; they cannot supply precision for total contrasts.
challenge_resolution.quote: the indirect effect of human–GenAI collaboration in the idea generation phase on novelty through cognitive flexibility was significant (estimate = 0.17, 95 % CI = [0.033, 0.341])
challenge_resolution.locator: p. 6, Sections 5.1.3 and 5.2.3; p. 8, Section 6.3.3; p. 9, Hypothesis 7

challenge_resolution.problem: S4-O2 names generation as treatment although the usefulness hypothesis tests collaboration during elaboration against generation.
challenge_resolution.what_changed: Swapped the usefulness contrast's treatment and control arms so elaboration is treatment and generation is control, with perceived-intelligence cells pooled within each. Changed direction to treatment_higher. Retained the printed r = 0.42 with CP coded 1 = elaboration; no effect size was calculated.
challenge_resolution.quote: human–GenAI collaboration in the idea elaboration phase (compared with the generation phase) improves creative usefulness by reducing cognitive overload.
challenge_resolution.locator: p. 1, Abstract; pp. 3-4, H5; p. 8, Table 3 and Section 6.3.3 (Hypothesis 5)

open_items.item: Original open question 1: Study 3 phase coding differs between Table 3/Section 6.3.1 (1 = elaboration) and H3 (1 = generation). Each analysis explicitly gives its coding, so the correlations and mediation are transcribed using their local definitions. No eligibility criterion depends on a common coding, and nothing further is needed for screening (p. 8).

Original open question 2 and unresolved reconciliation difference for studies[3].ai_tool.how_used: whether ChatGPT was blocked in Study 3's non-assigned phase remains unknown (p. 7, Section 6.1; p. 14, Appendices G-H). Authors' phase instructions and access rules would settle availability. This concerns implementation detail; the randomized assignment to different collaboration phases is explicit, so criterion 1 remains met.

Original open question 3: the exact proposal version scored, preliminary or final, is not explicitly identified (pp. 5-7, Sections 5.1.2 and 6.2). Authors can identify the submissions sent to experts. Either is participant-produced output, so criterion 3 is met; the uncertainty concerns timing and AI availability.

Original open question 4: Study 2a's elaboration develops AI-assisted preliminary ideas within the same creative proposal (p. 13, Appendices D-E). Retain with_ai for this continuing task; no separate unassisted task or later transfer test is reported. Study 3's unreported access rule is handled separately. No additional evidence is needed for eligibility.

Original open question 5: Study 3 lacks exact arm/cell sizes and arm-level outcome summaries (p. 8, Table 3). Authors' participant-level records or cell summaries would settle these; no data link is printed. Criterion 2 is already met by the explicit 198 people analyzed across all conditions.

Original open question 6: preregistered primary outcomes are unconfirmed because the external AsPredicted protocol is absent from the PDF and network retrieval failed (p. 7, Section 6.1). The linked protocol would settle primary-outcome status. The paper's randomization, analyzed sample size, and expert scoring already establish all three criteria.

Original open question 7: Studies 2a-2b give condition means, SDs, and within-person correlations but no paired total-effect test or standard error (pp. 6-7, Tables 1-2). Authors' analysis outputs would supply these if needed. Both studies are below 50 people and do not determine paper-level eligibility.

Original open question 8: Study 3 reports no direct novelty/usefulness contrast for the randomized perceived-intelligence factor; Table 3's PGenAII is the measured scale (pp. 7-9). Authors' factorial cell summaries or analysis outputs would settle an additional contrast. This does not affect the eligible phase-comparison evidence or any eligibility criterion.
